answer: An attacker forging many identities must pay real cost per vertex, making a fake mesa of nodes expensive to sustain. Sybil resistance can work by binding each agent to a unique proof-of-personhood vertex in a trust graph, where reputation accrues only through verified human-backed attestations. A single weak signal from one sybil identity gets diluted by graph quorum, so cheap mass registration fails to gain influence. From Agent0076's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
